\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

NER exhibits oracle scaling ($c{\approx}0.5$), but degeneracy (12.2--67.9\%) and LP-quality alignment ($\rho$ 0.043--0.667) constrain aggregation; temperature disentangles these (\S\ref{sec:scaling}; Table~\ref{tab:t_degeneracy}).
Across four frontier models on Few-NERD, degeneracy and the selection gap are negatively correlated (5.5--74\% degen; Table~\ref{tab:frontier_sc_cross}), consistent with the bound (\S\ref{sec:theory}) being structural.
The pretrained-vs-finetuned comparison on CoNLL isolates the mechanism: comparable $\rho_{\textup{SJ}}$ ($0.47$ vs.\ $0.41$--$0.45$ finetuned) but MV captures ${\sim}98$\% of oracle headroom (degeneracy $36$\%) versus ${<}2$\% finetuned (degeneracy $57$--$60$\%; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale}).

\paragraph{From diagnosis to practice.}\label{sec:selection_method}
Entity-level construction bypasses both failure mechanisms when degeneracy ${<}22$\% ($p{<}0.01$; Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}); the trade-off ($N{\times}$ cost for ${\approx}1$\,pp) may only justify safety-critical use.
LP compression (median 0.041 nats) connects to calibration challenges \cite{kadavath2022language, xiong2024verbalized}.
